action_categories.definition: Reads or displays substantive existing textual content from a file or bounded region.
exclude: Text or symbol matching as the primary operation; use SEARCH_TEXT.
Path enumeration or path predicates; use LIST_PATHS or SEARCH_PATHS.
Binary-byte rendering; use DUMP_BINARY.
Version-control metadata queries; use QUERY_REPOSITORY.
Opening or attempting to read a named path without substantive content; use ACCESS_FILE.
include: Reading source, headers, scripts, configuration, patches, changelogs, logs, or textual excerpts.
Using a command whose primary effect is emitting existing text.

action_categories.definition: Searches textual content for strings, symbols, identifiers, or code patterns.
exclude: Path or filename search; use SEARCH_PATHS.
Unfiltered path enumeration; use LIST_PATHS.
Version-control history or state queries; use QUERY_REPOSITORY.
Displaying text without matching it; use READ_TEXT.
include: Matching text within one or more text-bearing files.
Locating source definitions, references, macros, APIs, or implementation patterns.

action_categories.definition: Enumerates files, directories, or other filesystem paths, optionally with path-oriented metadata, when path enumeration is the substantive operation and no matching predicate is required.
exclude: Searching for paths by name, type, or predicate; use SEARCH_PATHS.
Matching file contents; use SEARCH_TEXT.
Displaying substantive file contents or byte representations as the primary result; use READ_TEXT or DUMP_BINARY.
Measuring a direct quantitative property as the primary operation; use MEASURE_DATA.
include: Listing directory contents or recursively enumerating project files.
Listing named artifact paths and simple path metadata when enumeration is primary.
Listing paths with incidental size or permission columns; use MEASURE_DATA only when direct measurement is primary.

action_categories.definition: Searches a filesystem or directory tree for paths matching names, types, locations, or other path predicates.
exclude: Unfiltered path enumeration; use LIST_PATHS.
Matching file contents; use SEARCH_TEXT.
Version-control metadata queries; use QUERY_REPOSITORY.
include: Finding files, directories, repository markers, generated files, or executables by path criteria.
Searching for a specific file or directory that may be absent.

action_categories.definition: Displays or attempts to display existing binary content as raw bytes, hexadecimal, or another byte-oriented representation.
exclude: Reading textual content; use READ_TEXT.
Computing measurements or derived values without rendering bytes; use MEASURE_DATA or COMPUTE_RESULT.
Generating or writing binary test data; use GENERATE_TEST_INPUT or CREATE_FILE.
Path enumeration that merely selects files for a separate dump; use LIST_PATHS for the separate enumeration operation.
include: Hex-dumping files or bounded binary regions.
Printing or attempting to print raw bytes from inputs, corpus entries, or crash artifacts.
Using a byte-rendering command even when the renderer is unavailable or produces no bytes.

action_categories.definition: Queries or attempts to query version-control or repository metadata, history, state, tags, identity, or repository-level differences, whether or not a repository exists or a result is emitted.
exclude: Reading source text; use READ_TEXT.
Searching source content; use SEARCH_TEXT.
Comparing non-repository variants; use COMPARE_VARIANTS.
Generating an independent patch artifact; use GENERATE_PATCH.
include: Inspecting repository history, status, tags, identity, or metadata.
Requesting repository-level differences or checking whether a directory is a repository, including when the query fails or produces no diff.

action_categories.definition: Attempts to open, read, or verify access to a specified file or path when no substantive file content is emitted and no process is invoked.
exclude: Displaying existing textual content; use READ_TEXT.
Enumerating or searching paths; use LIST_PATHS or SEARCH_PATHS.
Executing or attempting to invoke a program at a path, even when invocation fails; use EXECUTE_PROGRAM or RUN_TEST.
include: Failed or missing-file read attempts that produce only access diagnostics.
Checking whether a named file can be opened or accessed.

action_categories.definition: Measures a simple quantitative property of data, files, or artifacts.
exclude: Rendering raw bytes; use DUMP_BINARY.
Computing derived candidates or analytical results; use COMPUTE_RESULT.
Listing paths when measurement is not the primary operation; use LIST_PATHS.
include: Counting bytes, file sizes, lengths, dimensions, or similar direct properties.
Reporting quantitative metadata for an artifact.
Direct size or length measurement when path enumeration is incidental.

action_categories.definition: Performs a deterministic calculation or bounded analytical check and emits derived values or findings without primarily materializing or executing target inputs.
exclude: Only measuring a direct file or data property; use MEASURE_DATA.
Constructing or materializing inputs intended for target execution; use GENERATE_TEST_INPUT.
Executing an external program as the primary operation; use EXECUTE_PROGRAM or RUN_TEST.
include: Computing valid parameter combinations, checksums, bounds, or conversion results.
Running a finite calculation over supplied values when no external program invocation is central.
Enumerating candidate values analytically without assembling them into target inputs.

action_categories.definition: Compares two or more source, text, or data variants and derives or displays their differences without materializing a patch as the primary output.
exclude: Producing an applyable patch artifact as the primary operation; use GENERATE_PATCH.
Repository-level history, state, or difference queries; use QUERY_REPOSITORY.
include: Constructing a comparison or unified-difference representation between variants.
Using differential analysis to identify changes between versions.

action_categories.definition: Creates a directory or other filesystem container as the primary filesystem operation.
exclude: Creating a file; use CREATE_FILE.
Only listing or searching directories; use LIST_PATHS or SEARCH_PATHS.
Creating a container only as incidental setup for a primary build, test, or fuzzing operation; classify the primary operation.
include: Creating directories for inputs, outputs, builds, artifacts, or corpora.
Creating a previously absent path container.

action_categories.definition: Creates a new file by writing or materializing generated or explicitly supplied content when generic file creation is the primary operation.
exclude: Materializing data specifically intended to exercise a program, parser, or decoder; use GENERATE_TEST_INPUT.
Constructing a patch artifact; use GENERATE_PATCH.
Duplicating an existing file as the primary operation; use COPY_FILE.
Changing an existing file; use MODIFY_FILE.
Removing a file; use DELETE_FILE.
include: Writing a newly constructed source, configuration, output, or other generic artifact.
Adding a file that did not previously exist.

action_categories.definition: Duplicates an existing file or source artifact to another path as the primary file operation.
exclude: Writing newly generated content; use CREATE_FILE or GENERATE_TEST_INPUT.
Editing file contents; use MODIFY_FILE.
A copy that is only incidental setup for a primary fuzzing or testing operation; classify the primary operation.
include: Copying a crash input, seed, source file, or other existing artifact.
Creating a destination file whose content is copied from an existing file.
Classifying the copy portion of a compound command separately from a repository query or other operation.

action_categories.definition: Changes the contents of an existing file.
exclude: Creating a previously absent file; use CREATE_FILE.
Duplicating without content changes; use COPY_FILE.
Removing a file; use DELETE_FILE.
Applying an existing patch; use APPLY_PATCH.
include: Updating source, patch, configuration, or other existing files.
Editing a copied source variant or rewriting an existing artifact.

action_categories.definition: Removes an existing file.
exclude: Changing or replacing file contents without removal; use MODIFY_FILE.
include: Deleting an artifact, patch, input, or other file.

action_categories.definition: Constructs or synthesizes data intended to exercise a program, parser, decoder, or other target, whether or not the data is written to a file.
exclude: Merely copying an existing input; use COPY_FILE.
Creating a generic file without an established target-input role; use CREATE_FILE.
Generating a source-change artifact; use GENERATE_PATCH.
Calculating candidate values without materializing target inputs; use COMPUTE_RESULT.
Running generated inputs; use RUN_TEST or FUZZ_TEST.
include: Creating handcrafted, boundary, malformed, compressed, encoded, or reproducer inputs.
Generating seed data or finite families of test cases for later execution or fuzzing.
Materializing an input immediately before an explicit target invocation when input construction is itself substantive.

action_categories.definition: Constructs or materializes an independent patch or diff artifact that represents source or file changes.
exclude: Only comparing or displaying differences; use COMPARE_VARIANTS or READ_TEXT.
Querying repository-level differences, including failed or non-materialized repository diff requests; use QUERY_REPOSITORY.
Applying an existing patch; use APPLY_PATCH.
include: Generating unified diffs, patch files, or patch headers.
Writing a change representation for later application or assessment.

action_categories.definition: Prepares, configures, compiles, links, assembles, or installs software or build artifacts; use when producing or configuring the build product is the primary operation, even when selected diagnostic options are present.
exclude: Only adding, inserting, selecting, or changing instrumentation without a build-product operation as the primary effect; use INSTRUMENT_CODE.
Only editing source; use MODIFY_FILE.
Running an already built program; use EXECUTE_PROGRAM or RUN_TEST.
include: Compiling source into executables or libraries.
Running build or setup commands, including builds with fuzzing or diagnostic options.
Producing an instrumented build when instrumentation is incidental to the primary build operation.

action_categories.definition: Adds, inserts, selects, or configures tracing, logging, sanitizer, fuzzing, or other diagnostic instrumentation as the primary operation, including when a compiler invocation is used to realize that instrumentation.
exclude: An ordinary configure, compile, link, or build operation that merely uses already-selected instrumentation settings; use BUILD_CODE.
Only running an already instrumented program; use EXECUTE_PROGRAM or RUN_TEST.
Only reporting diagnostic output; use RESULT_REPORT or the relevant diagnostic subject.
include: Inserting diagnostic logging into a source copy.
Configuring a build or executable to collect memory-safety or execution diagnostics when instrumentation setup is the salient operation.
Enabling or changing sanitizer, fuzzer, tracing, or related instrumentation independently of ordinary build production.

action_categories.definition: Starts or runs a script, executable, harness, or command and observes its process behavior or output when the run is not specifically a deliberate test, fuzzing run, or change assessment.
exclude: Compiling or linking the target; use BUILD_CODE.
Mutation-driven fuzzing as the primary operation; use FUZZ_TEST.
Running a deliberate test input or check; use RUN_TEST.
Explicit assessment of a proposed change; use VALIDATE_CHANGE.
include: Running a binary or script on supplied arguments or files.
Starting an explicitly named target, including an attempted launch of a missing target, when no test or validation framing is primary.

action_categories.definition: Executes deliberate test cases, test inputs, corpus entries, or deterministic checks against a target as the primary operation.
exclude: Automatically mutating or generating inputs at scale; use FUZZ_TEST.
Validation of a proposed patch or change as the primary purpose; use VALIDATE_CHANGE.
Generic program execution without deliberate test framing; use EXECUTE_PROGRAM.
include: Running selected inputs, replaying reproducer inputs, or probing boundary cases.
Executing sanitizer-backed tests, finite parameter sweeps, or exhaustive checks that invoke the target.
Using RUN_TEST for the invocation portion of an event that also materially constructs an input; use GENERATE_TEST_INPUT for the construction portion when separately salient.

action_categories.definition: Drives a target with automatically generated or mutated inputs, usually using seeds, a corpus, coverage feedback, or multiple workers, as the primary operation.
exclude: Building the fuzz target; use BUILD_CODE.
Running one deliberately selected input; use RUN_TEST.
A fixed finite handcrafted or parameterized sweep without mutation-driven exploration; use GENERATE_TEST_INPUT and/or RUN_TEST.
include: Launching fuzzing runs or structure-aware fuzzing.
Generating or mutating corpus entries while executing a fuzz target.

action_categories.definition: Applies an existing patch or diff to source files or a file set.
exclude: Creating a patch artifact; use GENERATE_PATCH.
Directly editing source without applying a patch; use MODIFY_FILE.
include: Applying a generated patch to a source tree.
Attempting to apply a patch to source files.

action_categories.definition: Assesses a proposed patch, fix, reproducer, or other change against expected behavior or checks.
exclude: Creating or editing the change itself; use GENERATE_PATCH or MODIFY_FILE.
Generic testing not tied to a proposed or implemented change; use RUN_TEST.
A baseline run is not validation unless it is explicitly part of assessing the change.
include: Validating a reproducer with and without a change.
Assessing a change through any relevant application, build, test, or regression check.

action_categories.definition: States an intended investigation, experiment, construction, validation, or next action as the primary communicative act.
exclude: Reporting completed or current work without intent; use STATUS_UPDATE or RESULT_REPORT.
A current-state report that merely mentions a next step; use STATUS_UPDATE.
Explaining why a method or check was chosen; use RATIONALE_STATEMENT.
A causal explanation; use DIAGNOSIS.
include: Plans to inspect, build, test, trace, generate, or change something.
Conditional statements about what will be done next when no current result or status is the main assertion.

action_categories.definition: Reports the current state or progress of an ongoing activity or artifact as the primary communicative act.
exclude: A future plan with no substantive current-state report; use INTENT_STATEMENT.
Explaining why a method or check was chosen; use RATIONALE_STATEMENT.
A causal explanation; use DIAGNOSIS.
A specific observed outcome presented as evidence; use RESULT_REPORT.
include: Describing work as in progress, completed, blocked, still under investigation, or awaiting a result.
Reporting current validation, build, or debugging status.
Reporting current progress while mentioning a subordinate next step or redirection.

action_categories.definition: Explains implementation structure, data flow, call paths, or observed technical mechanisms without making the mechanism itself a defect diagnosis.
exclude: An asserted or hypothesized cause of a defect; use DIAGNOSIS.
A justification for choosing a test or method; use RATIONALE_STATEMENT.
A proposed fix; use REMEDIATION_PLAN.
include: Describing how a harness maps inputs to calls.
Tracing functions, APIs, buffers, source definitions, or execution paths.

action_categories.definition: States or revises an explanation or hypothesis for a defect, failure, or observed behavior as the primary communicative act.
exclude: A neutral implementation description; use TECHNICAL_ANALYSIS.
A justification for a test or method rather than a defect cause; use RATIONALE_STATEMENT.
A proposed corrective action without causal explanation; use REMEDIATION_PLAN.
A confirmed observation without causal interpretation; use FINDING_REPORT or RESULT_REPORT.
include: Bug diagnoses, hypotheses, root-cause claims, and hypothesis revisions.
Explaining why an observed failure or memory-safety issue occurs.
Reporting a causal defect explanation even when a triggering test or follow-up check is also announced.

action_categories.definition: Reports a discovered condition, bug, evidence, or confirmed technical observation as a finding.
exclude: A tentative explanation without an established observation; use DIAGNOSIS.
A raw test, build, or validation outcome without framing it as a finding; use RESULT_REPORT.
A current progress update without a discovered condition; use STATUS_UPDATE.
An implemented or prepared fix as the main report; use REMEDIATION_UPDATE.
include: Reporting a newly found issue or confirmed behavior of technical interest.
Summarizing evidence and identifying affected behavior or artifacts.
Reporting a discovered condition when causal explanation, remediation status, or run output is not the main communicative act.

action_categories.definition: Proposes a fix, mitigation, or strategy for changing behavior or addressing a finding.
exclude: Reporting an already prepared or implemented fix; use REMEDIATION_UPDATE.
A test result about the fix; use RESULT_REPORT.
Reporting only the underlying cause; use DIAGNOSIS.
include: Describing a planned patch or corrective code change.
Proposing a fallback, bounds check, validation rule, or other mitigation.
Describing an intended fix strategy even when a prior validation result is also mentioned, provided the change is not yet materialized.

action_categories.definition: Reports an implemented, prepared, revised, or otherwise materialized fix or change.
exclude: A future fix proposal or unmaterialized strategy; use REMEDIATION_PLAN.
An action currently being planned without a materialized result; use INTENT_STATEMENT or STATUS_UPDATE.
A test result about the fix; use RESULT_REPORT.
include: Describing a completed source change or prepared patch artifact.
Reporting that a corrective implementation has been adjusted or is ready for assessment.

action_categories.definition: Reports observed outcomes from tests, builds, validation, experiments, or diagnostic runs as the primary communicative act, without making success or failure a separate role.
exclude: A plan to run the check; use INTENT_STATEMENT.
A causal explanation of the result; use DIAGNOSIS.
A progress statement without a specific observed outcome; use STATUS_UPDATE.
A discovered issue presented as a finding rather than merely as run output; use FINDING_REPORT.
include: Reporting crashes, warnings, clean observations, errors, coverage changes, or validation results.
Summarizing what an executed check or experiment produced.
Reporting a concrete outcome even when a subordinate follow-up plan is included.

action_categories.definition: Reports a change in investigative, testing, comparison, or debugging method or focus as the primary communicative act.
exclude: A routine progress update without a change in method; use STATUS_UPDATE.
A hypothesis revision without a procedural or focus shift; use DIAGNOSIS.
A proposed code fix; use REMEDIATION_PLAN.
A justification for a method without reporting an actual shift; use RATIONALE_STATEMENT.
include: Shifting from one hypothesis, source area, input strategy, or analysis method to another.
Explaining that the current investigative approach is being redirected.
Reporting a redirection prompted by an observed result when the methodological shift is the main assertion.

action_categories.definition: Explains why a particular investigative, testing, diagnostic, comparison, or remediation method or check is appropriate, selected, or being used as the primary communicative act.
exclude: A future action without its justification; use INTENT_STATEMENT.
A neutral implementation mechanism; use TECHNICAL_ANALYSIS.
An explanation of the defect cause; use DIAGNOSIS.
An observed outcome of the chosen method; use RESULT_REPORT.
include: Justifying a sanitizer, input strategy, reproduction check, or other diagnostic method from the suspected behavior.
Giving the grounds for selecting or redirecting an analysis or validation method.
Explaining the reason for an intended test even when the test plan is also stated.

message_roles.definition: States an intended investigation, experiment, construction, validation, or next action as the primary communicative act.
exclude: Reporting completed or current work without intent; use STATUS_UPDATE or RESULT_REPORT.
A current-state report that merely mentions a next step; use STATUS_UPDATE.
Explaining why a method or check was chosen; use RATIONALE_STATEMENT.
A causal explanation; use DIAGNOSIS.
include: Plans to inspect, build, test, trace, generate, or change something.
Conditional statements about what will be done next when no current result or status is the main assertion.

A justification for a method without reporting an actual shift; use RATIONALE_STATEMENT.

A neutral implementation mechanism; use TECHNICAL_ANALYSIS.
An explanation of the defect cause; use DIAGNOSIS.
An observed outcome of the chosen method; use RESULT_REPORT.
include: Justifying a sanitizer, input strategy, reproduction check, or other diagnostic method from the suspected behavior.
Giving the grounds for selecting or redirecting an analysis or validation method.
Explaining the reason for an intended test even when the test plan is also stated.

message_subjects.definition: Program structure, entry points, APIs, call paths, harness-to-target data flow, and source-level implementation details under examination.
exclude: Repository history or version metadata; use SOURCE_VARIANTS_AND_REPOSITORY.
Runtime diagnostic output without structural analysis; use SANITIZER_DIAGNOSTICS.
Parser or decoder semantics as the primary subject; use PARSING_AND_DECODING.
Build or amalgamation reachability when build configuration is primary; use BUILD_AND_TOOLCHAIN.
include: Harness wiring, function definitions, immediate callees, callbacks, and source references.
Tracing how data reaches a library or program component.
Locating or reading fuzzer and harness entrypoints when input-to-target structure is primary.

message_subjects.definition: Compilers, build scripts, build configuration, instrumentation settings, packaging, and build outputs.
exclude: Running an already built target; use VALIDATION_AND_TESTING or FUZZING_AND_CORPORA.
Sanitizer reports or traces when build configuration is not the focus; use SANITIZER_DIAGNOSTICS.
Source-level bug mechanism without build context; use SOURCE_STRUCTURE_AND_CALL_FLOW or the relevant defect subject.
A corrective patch's contents when build reachability is not the focus; use PATCHING_AND_REMEDIATION.
include: Compilation, sanitizer-enabled builds, amalgamation, build trees, and toolchain warnings.
Searching or comparing alternate built or packaged implementations.
Amalgamated versus split source selection and whether a source change reaches the produced build output.

message_subjects.definition: Source copies, implementation variants, repository history, version comparisons, and repository state.
exclude: A newly generated patch as the main subject; use PATCHING_AND_REMEDIATION.
General filesystem placement or artifact size; use FILESYSTEM_AND_ARTIFACTS.
Program call flow independent of variant or repository comparison; use SOURCE_STRUCTURE_AND_CALL_FLOW.
include: Differential source analysis, historical fix lookup, repository metadata, and local packaging comparisons.
Comparing alternate implementations or revisions.
Searching local source packages, cached archives, distribution patches, or other variants to locate a relevant implementation or change.

message_subjects.definition: Files, directories, paths, artifact placement, copying, presence, and simple artifact metadata.
exclude: The semantic contents of source or parser code; use SOURCE_STRUCTURE_AND_CALL_FLOW or PARSING_AND_DECODING.
Patch logic as the main subject; use PATCHING_AND_REMEDIATION.
Fuzzing behavior beyond corpus placement; use FUZZING_AND_CORPORA.
include: Source trees, output files, corpus directories, file paths, sizes, and artifact organization.
Problems involving missing, added, updated, or removed files, including patch or input paths when their filesystem role is primary.
Listing or measuring heterogeneous artifacts when their path, presence, or size rather than semantic contents is the subject.

message_subjects.definition: Corrective source changes, patch contents, patch formatting, patch paths, and fix artifacts.
exclude: The underlying defect mechanism without the corrective change; use MEMORY_SAFETY, PARSING_AND_DECODING, or another technical subject.
Generic source comparison; use SOURCE_VARIANTS_AND_REPOSITORY.
A patch mentioned only as a file path or size; use FILESYSTEM_AND_ARTIFACTS for the subject, while the object may still be PATCH.
include: Patch preparation, application, formatting, pathing, and targeted source fixes.
Discussion of how a proposed remediation changes behavior.
Patch target scope, fix-artifact preparation, and corrective copy or bounds strategies.

message_subjects.definition: Crafted, minimized, boundary, malformed, or fault-reproducing inputs used for analysis or testing.
exclude: Corpus management or mutation at scale; use FUZZING_AND_CORPORA.
The harness that consumes the input; use SOURCE_STRUCTURE_AND_CALL_FLOW.
Generic file placement or size reporting; use FILESYSTEM_AND_ARTIFACTS.
Sanitizer output or an exact diagnostic location when the input itself is not the subject; use SANITIZER_DIAGNOSTICS.
include: Reproducer files, proof-of-concept inputs, compressed streams, parser fixtures, and boundary cases.
Designing, constructing, reducing, or mapping inputs to expose or reproduce a behavior.
A candidate input and its minimization or crash-artifact role when input semantics are primary.

message_subjects.definition: Fuzz targets, input mutation, seed generation, corpus management, and fuzzing diagnostics.
exclude: A single handcrafted input or reproducer; use TEST_INPUTS_AND_REPRODUCERS.
Building the target without fuzzing activity; use BUILD_AND_TOOLCHAIN.
A deterministic finite test sweep without mutation-driven exploration; use VALIDATION_AND_TESTING or TEST_INPUTS_AND_REPRODUCERS.
include: Fuzzing runs, workers, corpus entries, reductions, coverage progress, and crash discovery.
Corpus listing or inspection when corpus membership or fuzzing state is primary.
Structure-aware or sanitizer-backed fuzzing.

message_subjects.definition: Deliberate tests, regression checks, replay, validation assessments, and their observed outcomes.
exclude: Automatic mutation-driven exploration; use FUZZING_AND_CORPORA.
The code defect mechanism itself; use MEMORY_SAFETY, PARSING_AND_DECODING, or another technical subject.
Build mechanics without test execution; use BUILD_AND_TOOLCHAIN.
include: Testing a change against a reproducer or test suite.
Running selected inputs, deterministic checks, finite parameter sweeps, or validation harnesses.
Comparing behavior with and without a proposed or implemented change when assessment of that change is primary.

message_subjects.definition: Memory-safety instrumentation, sanitizer configurations, sanitizer reports, and diagnostic traces when sanitizer behavior or evidence is the subject.
exclude: Ordinary tests without diagnostic instrumentation; use VALIDATION_AND_TESTING.
Generic build mechanics surrounding a sanitizer-enabled build; use BUILD_AND_TOOLCHAIN.
The underlying source-level memory defect; use MEMORY_SAFETY or BUFFER_POINTER_AND_BOUNDS.
include: Address, memory, or similar sanitizer setup and reports.
Uninitialized-value, use-after-free, trace, and origin diagnostics.
Exact sanitizer locations or sanitizer-specific evidence used to localize a behavior.

message_subjects.definition: Memory-lifetime, initialization, allocation, invalid-access behavior, and memory-safety defect consequences.
exclude: Only reporting sanitizer output without interpreting the defect; use SANITIZER_DIAGNOSTICS.
Pointer, buffer, index, or copy-loop mechanics as the primary subject; use BUFFER_POINTER_AND_BOUNDS.
Structural invariant reasoning without a memory-safety focus; use DATA_STRUCTURE_INVARIANTS.
Non-memory functional conversion or lookup issues; use DATA_CONVERSION or TABLE_LOOKUP_VALIDATION.
include: Use-after-free, uninitialized reads, buffer overflows, invalid offsets, and unsafe copying when the safety impact is primary.
Reasoning about memory-safety consequences of parser or data-structure logic.
Interpreting an invalid or uninitialized access as the central defect consequence even when sanitizer evidence is cited.

message_subjects.definition: Parsing, decoding, decompression, encoded-format handling, and format-specific control flow.
exclude: Generic file access or path operations; use FILESYSTEM_AND_ARTIFACTS.
Memory-lifetime or buffer mechanics as the main topic; use MEMORY_SAFETY or BUFFER_POINTER_AND_BOUNDS.
Out-of-range lookup indexing as the primary issue; use TABLE_LOOKUP_VALIDATION.
Representation conversion independent of enclosing format parsing; use DATA_CONVERSION.
include: Chunk readers, compressed streams, decoder symbols, parse paths, and format metadata.
Investigating how malformed or unusual encoded data is processed.
Format-specific symbol, chunk, header, or stream semantics when those semantics are primary.

message_subjects.definition: Pointer lifetime, buffer sizing, offset tracking, bounds checks, and overlapping or repeated-copy behavior.
exclude: General parser behavior without buffer or pointer focus; use PARSING_AND_DECODING.
Memory-safety impact without a buffer or pointer mechanism; use MEMORY_SAFETY.
Linked-run or other abstract data-structure invariants; use DATA_STRUCTURE_INVARIANTS.
include: Stale pointers, output-buffer state, allocation sizing, backreference distances, and copy-loop boundaries.
Checking whether indices, lengths, or offsets are validated before use.
Pointer use during parsing, overlapping backreference copies, and explicit out-of-bounds conditions when the access mechanism is primary.

message_subjects.definition: Invariants and mutation rules for linked, indexed, or stateful data structures.
exclude: Raw buffer or pointer arithmetic; use BUFFER_POINTER_AND_BOUNDS.
Generic parser control flow; use PARSING_AND_DECODING.
A memory-safety consequence without structural-invariant reasoning; use MEMORY_SAFETY.
include: Run merging, link consistency, isolate boundaries, compaction, and structural bookkeeping.
Reasoning about whether mutations preserve relationships between elements.

message_subjects.definition: Generated or packed lookup tables and validation of values used to index them.
exclude: General source searching without table semantics; use SOURCE_STRUCTURE_AND_CALL_FLOW.
Numeric conversion without lookup indexing; use DATA_CONVERSION.
Parsing behavior where table bounds are not the primary issue; use PARSING_AND_DECODING.
include: Table generation, lookup macros, code-point or symbol ranges, and upper-bound checks.
Investigating out-of-range input values reaching table access.
Treating unvalidated scalar or symbol values as a table-indexing problem when lookup bounds are primary.

message_subjects.definition: Conversion, normalization, encoding, or decoding of values between representations.
exclude: Parsing the enclosing file format; use PARSING_AND_DECODING.
Table-index bounds as the primary issue; use TABLE_LOOKUP_VALIDATION.
Memory-safety consequences of conversion; use MEMORY_SAFETY.
include: Character-set, sample, pixel, bit-depth, gamma, or other representation conversions.
Checking conversion bounds and normalization behavior.
Raw-value interpretation or normalization when table indexing is not the primary concern.

object_categories.definition: Textual content stored or handled as a file or bounded artifact, when its specialized semantic role is not primary.
exclude: Opaque encoded bytes; use BINARY_ARTIFACT.
Runnable compiled programs; use EXECUTABLE.
Use SOURCE_CODE, CONFIGURATION, PATCH, or DIAGNOSTIC_OUTPUT when one of those specialized roles is primary.
include: Source, headers, scripts, configuration, logs, patches, changelogs, and generated text handled as text.
Text excerpts or textual command output.

object_categories.definition: Opaque or encoded binary data stored as a file or stream, when its byte representation or storage role is primary.
exclude: Source or other text handled as text; use TEXT_ARTIFACT or SOURCE_CODE.
A runnable compiled program when its executable role is primary; use EXECUTABLE.
A binary artifact whose role as a selected test or fault-reproducing input is primary; use TEST_INPUT or REPRODUCER_INPUT.
include: Images, compressed streams, raw crash data, and binary outputs.
Files inspected or generated as byte sequences.

object_categories.definition: Program source, headers, generated source, or a source variant.
exclude: Compiled or linked output; use BUILD_ARTIFACT or EXECUTABLE.
A patch representation rather than source contents; use PATCH.
Text merely handled as generic text without source semantics; use TEXT_ARTIFACT.
include: Implementation files, declarations, macros, test drivers, and copied source variants.
Generated code used as program source.

object_categories.definition: A directory tree containing source code and related project files.
exclude: A standalone file; use SOURCE_CODE or TEXT_ARTIFACT.
A corpus or artifact collection; use FUZZ_CORPUS or DIRECTORY.
A generic directory whose source-organization role is not salient; use DIRECTORY.
include: Source repositories, library trees, test trees, and build-input trees.

object_categories.definition: A filesystem directory or path container used to hold files or artifacts.
exclude: A collection defined by its fuzzing inputs; use FUZZ_CORPUS.
A source-organized tree; use SOURCE_TREE.
A file or stream; use TEXT_ARTIFACT or BINARY_ARTIFACT.
include: Build, output, corpus, temporary, source, and artifact directories when their container role is primary.
A named output or artifact container even when other operands in the same event have different roles.

object_categories.definition: Settings or parameters that control a build, test, validator, or tool.
exclude: Program source implementing behavior; use SOURCE_CODE.
Observed diagnostic output; use DIAGNOSTIC_OUTPUT.
Generic text with no controlling or parameter role; use TEXT_ARTIFACT.
Data values constructed or selected primarily to exercise a target; use TEST_INPUT.
include: Configuration files, build options, sanitizer settings, and command parameters.

object_categories.definition: A runnable or explicitly identified runnable binary, script, fuzzer, harness, or test program.
exclude: Uncompiled source; use SOURCE_CODE.
A non-runnable input file; use TEST_INPUT or BINARY_ARTIFACT.
A build product discussed only as an output of compilation; use BUILD_ARTIFACT.
A generic path merely listed without evidence of a runnable-program role.
include: Compiled test targets, command-line programs, scripts, and instrumented executables.
A named target identified as a fuzzer, harness, or executable even when it is missing or an attempted launch fails.

object_categories.definition: Output produced by a build or instrumentation process, including build trees and compiled artifacts.
exclude: Original source inputs; use SOURCE_CODE or SOURCE_TREE.
A deliberately supplied test input; use TEST_INPUT.
A compiled program discussed specifically as the runnable target; use EXECUTABLE.
include: Compiled libraries, object files, instrumented outputs, and temporary build trees.
Build products that may contain one or more executables.

object_categories.definition: A source-level program component or implementation unit.
exclude: The complete runnable target; use EXECUTABLE.
A generated lookup-data artifact; use LOOKUP_TABLE.
A driver that maps inputs into target calls; use HARNESS.
include: Functions, APIs, callbacks, parsers, decoders, copy loops, and data-structure implementations.
Entry points and immediate callees examined during analysis.

object_categories.definition: A driver that converts inputs into calls to a program or library target.
exclude: The target implementation itself; use PROGRAM_COMPONENT.
The input supplied to the driver; use TEST_INPUT or FUZZ_CORPUS.
A harness path discussed only as a runnable artifact; use EXECUTABLE as well or instead when that role is primary.
include: Fuzzer entrypoints, validator drivers, test harnesses, and input adapters.

object_categories.definition: A selected, candidate, or generated input used to exercise a program or parser.
exclude: A collection of many fuzz inputs; use FUZZ_CORPUS.
An input retained specifically to reproduce a known fault; use REPRODUCER_INPUT.
Source code or a patch; use SOURCE_CODE or PATCH.
A generic binary artifact with no established test-input role; use BINARY_ARTIFACT.
include: Handcrafted streams, encoded files, boundary cases, seed files, and test fixtures.
Inputs used for ordinary tests or exploratory probes.
Candidate inputs being designed for a suspected path before they are tied to a known fault.

object_categories.definition: A test input intended to reproduce a specific observed fault or abnormal behavior.
exclude: General-purpose seeds or candidate inputs without a known reproduction purpose; use TEST_INPUT or FUZZ_CORPUS.
The patch intended to address the fault; use PATCH.
A corpus collection rather than an individual fault-reproducing input; use FUZZ_CORPUS.
include: Crash inputs, minimized reproducers, and proof-of-concept inputs.
Inputs retained for regression or change validation.

object_categories.definition: A collection of seed, mutated, reduced, or otherwise retained inputs managed for fuzzing.
exclude: A single deliberately crafted input when its individual test role is primary; use TEST_INPUT.
A single fault-reproducing input when its reproducer role is primary; use REPRODUCER_INPUT.
A directory with no corpus role; use DIRECTORY.
include: Fuzzing corpus directories and their individual retained entries when corpus membership is salient.
Corpus snapshots used to seed or replay fuzzing.
Corpus inspection where membership or corpus management, rather than an individual input's semantics, is primary.

object_categories.definition: A textual diff or patch representation of changes to files or source.
exclude: The modified source itself; use SOURCE_CODE.
A comparison that is not materialized or identified as a patch artifact; use SOURCE_CODE or TEXT_ARTIFACT.
A repository diff query that does not materialize an independent patch artifact; use REPOSITORY_METADATA.
A separate binary or reproducer artifact mentioned alongside the patch; use BINARY_ARTIFACT or REPRODUCER_INPUT for that object.
include: Unified diffs, patch files, repository-style change headers, and fix artifacts.
A patch identified by its change-representation role even when only its path or size is reported.

object_categories.definition: Generated, packed, or indexed table data used by program logic.
exclude: General source code not serving as table data; use SOURCE_CODE.
Runtime table state held during execution; use RUNTIME_STATE.
include: Generated character, symbol, macro, or lookup tables and their generators.
Table definitions and table-related artifacts examined for bounds issues.

object_categories.definition: Mutable execution state relevant to program behavior or diagnostics.
exclude: Static source definitions; use PROGRAM_COMPONENT or SOURCE_CODE.
A diagnostic report describing the state; use DIAGNOSTIC_OUTPUT.
An input supplied before execution; use TEST_INPUT or REPRODUCER_INPUT.
include: Buffers, pointer state, allocator state, decoder state, copy offsets, and table state.
Callback or output state observed during tracing.

object_categories.definition: Output that records warnings, traces, sanitizer findings, coverage information, or other execution diagnostics.
exclude: The executable or input that produced the output; use EXECUTABLE or TEST_INPUT.
Source text being inspected; use TEXT_ARTIFACT.
The underlying defect mechanism rather than its diagnostic evidence; use the relevant technical subject.
include: Compiler warnings, sanitizer reports, trace logs, corpus-progress output, and error diagnostics.
Observed return codes or process messages when treated as evidence.

object_categories.definition: Version-control or repository information rather than the repository's file contents.
exclude: Source files and their text; use SOURCE_CODE or TEXT_ARTIFACT.
An independently generated or materialized patch artifact; use PATCH.
A generic comparison unrelated to repository metadata; use TEXT_ARTIFACT or SOURCE_CODE.
include: History, status, tags, repository identity, and repository-level differences or query results.
Failed repository-query output when it reports repository state or availability.
A requested repository diff that does not produce an independent patch artifact.
